points.headline: Anthropic goes public near a $2T valuation.
points.body: Priced at $83 a share, Anthropic opened on Nasdaq at $111, about a third higher, in the biggest IPO on record. Dario Amodei used the opening bell to recommit to pacing AI development, while analysts point to its huge compute commitments and cheaper open models as the risks.

points.headline: Agents that run your Mac arrive.
points.body: Google's Gemini app can now use a Mac for you, organizing files, filling out forms and handling multistep workflows. A job listing shows Apple is building its own agent that browses, works across apps and writes code, and Google says it tests its Chrome agents in a giant mirror copy of the internet so they cannot go rogue while learning.

points.headline: Meta's Muse agent mixes up private conversations.
points.body: Internal chats show Meta staff alarmed that Muse surfaced requests they never made and showed bank and bitcoin balances, which Meta says are not real data. The reports land as Meta readies Muse Charm, a small screen gadget for the agent reportedly priced at $300.

points.headline: Google adds Gemini 4 Neon and opens Genie 4.
points.body: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Neon, the latest member of the element-named Gemini 4 family, and made its Genie 4 world model available. Developers say the growing lineup makes it even harder to tell which model and price fit a job.

points.headline: AI now drives both sides of security.
points.body: The European Commission took HR and medical systems offline to contain an AI-assisted cyberattack. On defense, AI tools found more critical bugs in NGINX, and PostgreSQL 19 shipped two months late because of the flood of AI-reported vulnerabilities.

points.headline: Robotaxis push into Europe as Waymo pulls back.
points.body: Wayve, Stellantis and Nvidia are working with the French government on autonomous driving, and Bolt plans Stellantis robotaxi trials in Greater Paris from 2028. In the US, Waymo suspended driverless rides on high-speed roads nationwide after California ordered it off freeways following construction-zone incidents.
